items.question: Why did the Nickelena's captain not notice the crane boom striking the Mackinac Bridge while he was steering the tug under the span?
items.expected_answer: The premise is wrong: the captain was not steering. He was still in his stateroom when the tow passed under the bridge at 0213; a crewmember was at the helm, and the captain learned of the problem only when the engineer went below to notify him.

evidence.quote: At 0213, while he was still in his stateroom, the crewmember at the helm guided the vessel and barge under the Mackinac Bridge’s suspension span at 8 knots within the marked channel.
The engineer went below and notified the captain.

items.notes: Tests whether the system rejects the false premise that the captain was at the wheel during the bridge passage.

items.question: Roughly how far behind the Nickelena was the barge BMI 209 being pulled during its trip from Escanaba toward Sault Ste. Marie?
items.expected_answer: About 500 feet; once out of the harbor the captain had the tow line lengthened to about 500 feet for the voyage.

evidence.quote: Once the towing vessel and the barge were out of the harbor, the captain ordered the length of the tow line be increased to about 500 feet for the voyage

items.notes: Tests retrieval of a single narrative fact (tow line length) phrased without the report's wording.
